newsitem.title: UK: C&W set for telecoms merger - paper.
newsitem.headline: C&W set for telecoms merger - paper.

text.p: Cable and Wireless Plc will publish its offer document on Monday for the formation and flotation of Cable and Wireless Communications (C&WC), the Financial Times said.

The planned subsidiary, valued at about 5.0 billion stg ($7.98 billion) is aimed at revitalising Britain's stagnant cable television business and adding competition to the telecoms market, the newspaper said.

C&WC would be formed from C&W's subsidiary Mercury Communications together with UK quoted companies Nynex CableComms, Bell CableMedia and Videotron -- in a deal the newspaper described as one of the most complex mergers seen in the UK.
The offer document would set out the terms under which investors in Nynex CableComms and Bell CableMedia would be able to switch their holdings into C&WC shares.
The Financial Times said C&WC would be the UK's largest cable company and would be one of the few telephone companies in a position to challenge British Telecommuncations Plc.
Some 15 percent of the company would be floated in London and New York in late April or early May, the newspaper said.
